Parent Partnership Policy
At the end of 2025, we updated our Parent Partnership Policy which you will find below.
Over the course of the last 12 months, we have reviewed the old Parent ‘Codes of Conduct’ and with the help of teachers, parents/carers, Local Governors and Trustees, we have produced an updated HWLP Parent Partnership Policy.
In creating this new Trust-wide approach to working in partnership with parents/carers we have enlisted the help of the UK’s biggest parent charity ‘Parentkind’. We will be working alongside them over the course of this new year as we recognise how important it is to have positive parent-school partnerships both for the wellbeing and academic progress of our children.
Our recent Trust INSET day in November 2025 was dedicated to this topic and the whole staff body was involved in looking at strategies to further support communication and relationships.

Headteacher's Welcome
Dear Parents, Carers and Pupils,
Welcome to Thames Ditton Junior School – a progressive, ambitious school in the heart of Elmbridge.
At TDJS, we are unapologetically focused on what works best for children. We don’t follow trends or stick with methods just because “that’s the way it’s always been done.” Every decision we make is deliberate, based on research, and designed to give our pupils the strongest possible start in life.
When you visit us, you’ll see this in action:
We’re ambitious for every child—not just in what they achieve here, but in the strong foundations they take forward into the next stage of their education. TDJS is a safe and happy place where pupils thrive and flourish, thanks to the excellent pastoral care and support they receive.
Our journey as a school has been one of reflection, challenge, and growth. We are proud of how far we’ve come, but we’re never standing still. Every element of our curriculum, our teaching, and our approach is the result of deliberate design and intentionality—always evolving to ensure it makes the greatest possible difference for our pupils.
Our staff team is dedicated, hard-working, and united by a shared commitment to excellence and care. We model what it means to be human: we work hard, we make mistakes, and we learn from them.
If you’re looking for a school where every decision is carefully considered, where we’re always improving and building for the future, we’d love to welcome you. Please contact the school office to arrange a visit.
All the best, Matt Lewis Headteacher

Platinum Sports Award
We are delighted to share with you the fantastic news that once again TDJS has been awarded the prestigious School Games Platinum Award for participation and contribution to sport in 2025-2026.
The School Games Mark is a Government led award scheme launched in 2012, facilitated by the Youth Sport Trust to reward schools for their commitment to the development of competition across their school and into the community, and we are delighted to have been recognised for our success.
Every year, schools can apply to be considered for bronze/silver/ gold award marks from School Games. The School Games adjudicators, judge each school against stringent criteria in these areas of sports; participation, higher level competitions, inclusive festivals and clubs, before determining the suitable award level. If you reach the criteria for the Gold mark, you are then eligible to submit a further application for the Platinum award.
This is no mean feat, as the Platinum Mark is only awarded to a handful of schools nationwide who have consistently demonstrated a consistent dedication to sport and activity within their primary school.
We are immensely proud of all our pupils and staff for their continued dedication to all aspects of school sport and exercise.
None of this would be possible without the tireless work of Mrs Charlton who dedicates countless hours to providing opportunities for children to access sport. Her dedication, passion and hard work are a huge asset to our school and this award is an ongoing recognition of her hard work.

25 years at TDJS
This week we celebrate the 25th TDJS employee anniversary of Mrs Gardiner! Becky has worked under six Headteachers during her tenure and started her journey with us in the Specialist Centre. The move to the school office came a few years later and although she loves her role, Becky says she misses the interaction with the children, hence why she always volunteers to attend the annual residential trips. Some of Becky's official staff photos are included - you've hardly changed at all Mrs Gardiner!
Becky's anecdotes are fascinating, including the following:
When I first started in the office we had a typewriter, a fax machine and a banda machine – this was before photocopiers… you had to type the original on a special sheet and then roll off the copies. A nightmare of purply ink – and of course if your page had a spelling mistake you had to do it all again!! After that we had a photocopier that was so big it had its own room!
The school was also much smaller. The current Y3 and Y6 classrooms didn't exist and 5B and 5DS had only just been built. There was also no music lodge, no astro nor pavillion.
Becky's official staff photos over the years are above - you've hardly changed at all Mrs Gardiner! We are very grateful to have Becky at the heart of our TDJS family and wish her many congratulations on this enormous milestone.

MLD Specialist Centre
TDJS has a specialist MLD (Moderate Learning Difficulties) provision within the school. We have 16 spaces for children with special educational needs or disabilities and pupils who attend our provision have a primary need of moderate learning difficulties and/or speech and language difficulties.
All children in the centre provision have an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) and children who have a ‘specialist provision within a mainstream school’ in Section I of their EHCP may be suitable for a space within this setting. In order to be placed at TDJS MLD Centre, your case worker at the local authority would liaise with the admissions team at Surrey who may send us a consultation.
The children within the centre are usually working at least two years below their chronological age at the start of year 3 (approximately Reception to Year 1 level).
The purpose of the centre is to ensure that children are given the chance to reach their potential at a level suitable for their needs, develop life skills, gain independence and grow their self-advocacy skills.
The children access a high level of quality instruction through specialised teaching within their class in the centre. This has a higher ratio of adults: children than the mainstream classrooms and offers a flexible, bespoke approach to learning that suits the levels of our learners
The timetable in the morning mirrors that of the mainstream and the children access phonics tuition, writing, reading and maths. This is taught in a way that better-supports their needs and includes the use of Makaton, colourful semantics and multi-sensory approaches to learning. This helps to create memorable moments for the pupils thereby promoting their speech and readiness to learn.
All pupils work in small groups, led by a specialist SEND teacher and supported by adults. Input is given to the children as a class and then children’s learning is scaffolded and adapted depending on their specific needs. They would be supported in a small group by a member of the centre team following the class input.
In the afternoons, there is a flexible and individualised approach to the children joining their mainstream classes. For some children, they may access the majority of their learning in the mainstream in the afternoons. For others, they may build up to this slowly and for some children, they may go into the mainstream for accessible subjects such as music, art and PE. The children have adult support in the afternoons and this may also include children from the mainstream. This helps to develop the children’s integration within the mainstream class and also helps develop the children’s confidence, conversation and social skills
Each morning, before lunch, the children participate in a pre-teaching session to enable them to access the learning in the mainstream inclusion lesson. This will help to consolidate prior learning and expose children to subject-specific vocabulary. These lessons may also be differentiated so that they are more accessible to the pupils.
If a child needs additional support, we have access to advice from outside agencies. Some of the outside agencies that we work with include Occupational Therapy, Physiotherapy and the Physical and Sensory Support Service. We also have a Speech and Language Therapist and assistant who work with us on a weekly basis.
There is also more information about Surrey's Local Offer, the online hub for 0-25-year olds with special educational needs or a disability, on their website. Please click on the website link here www.surreylocaloffer.org.uk
Applications for children seeking a place at our Specialist Centre Provision need to have a specialist provision listed in section I of their EHCP. Applications go through the children’s local authority case worker and are not dealt with by the school’s admissions team.
Following a consultation with the Local Authority, any applications will be considered by the school and the case officer will notify parents of the outcome. The provision in the specialist centre is personalised and is not available to children experiencing difficulties in the mainstream setting, although resources and expertise are shared.
Admission Criteria for the MLD Provision (Specialist Centre)
The Centre can admit 16 pupils aged between Year 3 and Year 6. This equates to approximately 4 pupils in each year group and we generally take on 4 new pupils each September in Year 3. Further assessments of each pupil's needs are conducted; therefore, the admission criteria are broad rather than prescriptive.

The staff in the MLD provision at TDJS use strategies that are helpful to such pupils but the centre may not be a suitable provision for those who have a primary diagnosis of ASD.
We are able to offer tours of our centre to prospective parents, please email the school office if you would be interested in attending a tour. Please refer to our Key Documents page for the latest SEND policies.

Reading
Reading Canon at TDJS
At Thames Ditton Junior School, we value reading as a key life skill. By the time the children leave, they should be confident at selecting and reading a wide range of materials and enjoy regularly reading for pleasure. We have taken a considerable amount of time in creating a book canon that promotes a love of reading, has a well-structured progression of challenging literature and includes quality texts that will enrich teaching and learning. Our canon is designed and pitched with a broad, inclusive and ambitious range of books with themes that will enable children to become thoughtful, empathetic and informed citizens, where they have a good understanding of the diversities and complexities of the world around them.
We believe that this rich reading diet will equip the children with the tools to tackle unfamiliar vocabulary and material, which in turn will improve their own scheme of known words, improve spelling and improve grammar. This will lay the groundwork for effective communication in all subjects.
